pharm: Selective peripheral histamine H1-receptor antagonist; non-sedating, not metabolized (no CYP involvement), excreted largely unchanged.
quick: 20 mg PO once daily (children 6-11y, >=20 kg: 10 mg once daily)
Empty stomach - 1 h before or 2 h after food/juice
Avoid; data limited, preferable to avoid
No dose adjustment (excreted unchanged but exposure modest)
May add to CNS effects; caution
summary: Bilastine is a non-sedating second-generation H1-antihistamine for allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and urticaria. It is notable for negligible metabolism (no CYP), no clinically relevant cardiac (QT) effect at therapeutic doses, and little CNS penetration, so sedation is minimal. Food and fruit juices markedly reduce its absorption, so it must be taken on an empty stomach. It is approved in the EU and many other countries but is NOT FDA-approved.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (seasonal and perennial)
Symptomatic treatment of urticaria (including chronic spontaneous urticaria)

dosage.n: Take 1 h before or 2 h after food or fruit juice

admin: Take on an empty stomach: 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal
Do not take with fruit juice or other beverages that inhibit OATP1A2 (reduces absorption substantially)
Swallow tablet with water; orodispersible forms placed on tongue and allowed to disperse
Take at the same time each day for consistent symptom control
moa: Selective, peripherally acting antagonist of the histamine H1 receptor with high affinity and slow dissociation; blocks histamine-mediated effects (vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, pruritus). Poor blood-brain barrier penetration limits central H1 occupancy and sedation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to bilastine or any excipient
relative: Concomitant use with P-glycoprotein inhibitors in patients with moderate-to-severe renal impairment
Conditions predisposing to QT prolongation (caution despite low intrinsic risk)

preg: Limited human data; as a precaution avoid bilastine during pregnancy unless clearly necessary (EMA/SmPC).
lact: Excretion in human milk is unknown; a decision to discontinue breastfeeding or the drug should weigh benefit to the infant and the mother.
renal: No dose adjustment of bilastine itself is needed, but avoid co-administration with P-gp inhibitors in moderate/severe renal impairment because plasma levels may rise.
hepatic: No dose adjustment required; bilastine is not hepatically metabolized and exposure is not increased in hepatic impairment.

major: P-glycoprotein inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin, ciclosporin, ritonavir, diltiazem) - increase bilastine plasma levels
moderate: Other CNS depressants and alcohol (possible additive sedation)
Drugs that prolong QT interval (theoretical caution)
minor: None of clinical significance via CYP (bilastine is not metabolized)
interactions.food: Food reduces oral bioavailability by ~30%; grapefruit and other fruit juices reduce absorption via OATP1A2 inhibition - take on an empty stomach.
interactions.alcohol: May potentiate CNS effects; caution with concurrent use.
interactions.diagnostics: Discontinue several days before allergy skin (prick) testing to avoid false-negative results.

monitoring: Caution if co-administered with QT-prolonging agents or P-gp inhibitors
counsel: Take once daily on an empty stomach - 1 hour before or 2 hours after food
Do not take with fruit juice; it reduces how well the drug works
Sedation is uncommon, but use caution driving until you know how it affects you
Avoid combining with alcohol or other sedatives
Stop antihistamines a few days before scheduled allergy skin testing
pk: Store below 30 C in original packaging
pearls: Not metabolized by CYP enzymes - few drug-drug interactions and no hepatic dose adjustment
Food and fruit juices cut absorption sharply; empty-stomach dosing is essential
Among the least sedating and most cardiac-neutral (no QT effect) of the second-generation antihistamines at therapeutic dose
Substrate of P-glycoprotein - avoid P-gp inhibitors in renal impairment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on an empty stomach; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the once-daily schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific antidote; experience is limited. Manage symptomatically and supportively, monitoring cardiovascular status. Bilastine has shown no clinically relevant QT effect even at multiples of the therapeutic dose in studies.
